items.name: Absence
items.description: Voidborn stealth shuttle. Difficult to detect, difficult to explain.
items.lore:
The Absence doesn't hide — it simply becomes less relevant to nearby
sensors. Voidborn stealth technology doesn't cloak or jam; it operates on
a principle the Collective calls "perceptual displacement," which they
decline to elaborate on. The shield array draws more power than ships twice
this size, leaving almost no room for cargo or fuel reserves. Other empires'
detection equipment occasionally registers an Absence as a cosmic ray artifact
or background noise. The cabin is always three degrees too cold.

items.name: Absolute Entropy
items.description: Voidborn phase-shift ice harvester. Shield-wrapped, fragile-hulled, and disturbingly effective.
items.lore: The extraction system reaches through the surface of an ice body without disturbing it, pulling target materials directly from the interior. The technique leaves ice formations structurally intact — afterward, the only evidence of extraction is a slight drop in ambient temperature that instruments can measure but cannot explain. The shield array is the heaviest of any ice harvester in production, and necessarily so: dimensional phase-extraction generates feedback that would collapse an unshielded hull. The ship underneath the shields is fragile enough that this is not a theoretical concern. The name refers to the heat death state that the extraction zone locally approximates for a fraction of a second — conditions that should not exist outside mathematical models, applied to ice harvesting as routine procedure.

items.name: Absolute Zero
items.description: Solarian modular ice extraction platform. High CPU, open slots, configurable for any ice operation.
items.lore: Most ice harvesters ship fully committed — every slot filled, every watt allocated. The Absolute Zero ships with a harvester and a shield booster, then gets out of the way. The modular bus architecture underwent two years of peer review before the materials science division signed off, and what emerged was a platform that accommodates whatever the ice field demands: additional harvesters, crystallographic analyzers, cargo expansion. The shield layer compensates for the complete absence of weapons — a design choice that survived every review committee because the fitting budget it freed up justified itself. The Confederacy built a framework, not a finished product.

items.name: Accretion
items.description: Voidborn gas harvester. The organic membrane absorbs and compresses nebula gas to half its volume.
items.lore: The Accretion-class does not scoop gas so much as inhale it. The organic collection membrane extends from the hull like a vast translucent lung, and pilots suspect the membrane channels some of the nebula's energy directly into the shield grid — the Accretion runs the strongest shields of any gas harvester in production. Twin harvester arrays and the deepest fitting budget in its class give pilots more room to customize than any competitor. Non-Voidborn engineers who have examined the membrane describe its structure as "disturbingly pulmonary."

items.name: Accumulator
items.description: Nebula bulk gas collection and compression vessel. Enormous intake, stores compressed gas for transport.
items.lore:
The Accumulator-class was designed by the same Federation accounting
department that produces all their best ships. Enormous intake scoops
channel gas into compression tanks that store collected gas at densities
other empires' safety regulators would reject. One thousand twenty
cargo capacity carries both raw and compressed gas — the Federation
hauls everything and lets the station-side brokers sort out pricing.
Unarmed because guns don't generate revenue. The Accumulator doesn't
care about purity or processing — it cares about volume, and it has
more of it than anyone.

items.name: Aether
items.description: Solarian gas harvester. Pressurized tanks compress collected gases to half their normal volume.
items.lore: Named for the classical element once believed to fill the heavens, the Aether-class mounts two gas harvesting arrays where most ships carry one. The proprietary atmospheric intake system — fourteen months in development — yields more gas per collection pass than any competing design. The onboard spectrometer identifies compositions to nine decimal places, six more than required. Every utility slot is spoken for by the time the Aether leaves the shipyard, leaving pilots a single defense mount for personal preference. The design team submitted the loadout as a solved problem. No one has filed a rebuttal.

items.name: All Mine
items.description: Outer Rim mining capital. An entire mining operation welded onto a jump drive. Ugly, stubborn, effective.
items.lore: All Mine is an entire mining operation welded onto a jump drive. Held together by structural bracing, duct tape, and frontier stubbornness. The cheapest T5 industrial vessel by a wide margin, because the Rim builds capital ships the same way it builds everything: from whatever's available. Twenty-six hundred and forty cargo capacity hauls everything a remote mining operation produces. Two weapon mounts because the frontier is the frontier, and mining bases attract pirates. All Mine can operate independently for extended periods — no station docking required. It is, in every sense, a self-contained mining colony that happens to have engines.

items.name: Alloy Synthesizer
items.description: Voidborn dimensional alloy forge. Combines multiple ore types into advanced alloys in a single step.
items.lore:
The Alloy Synthesizer-class combines multiple raw ore types into
advanced alloys through dimensional compression that skips intermediate
refining stages entirely. Feed it iron, titanium, and null matter, and
the synthesis chambers produce alloys with crystal structures that
should require planetary-scale foundries. The Collective's materials
scientists describe the process as "showing matter the shape it wants
to take." Processing cycles are slow — each synthesis requires
dimensional stabilization that takes time — but a single step replaces
three conventional refining stages. Other empires cannot replicate
the process because it requires dimensional phase states they cannot
generate.

items.name: Analysis
items.description: Solarian armored salvager. Tough enough to work wreck sites in contested space. Pulse laser for self-defense.
items.lore: The Confederacy's salvage safety board reviewed incident reports from wreck-site operations and concluded that most losses came from debris impacts and opportunistic attacks during recovery. The Analysis was redesigned accordingly: reinforced hull plating, a default armor package, and a pulse laser for self-defense. The armor drops speed, which the safety board accepted — a salvager that arrives slowly and survives is preferable to one that arrives quickly and doesn't. Every recovered component is still scanned, catalogued, and assessed for reuse potential. The Confederacy didn't remove the methodical part. They just armored it.

items.name: Annihilation
items.description: Voidborn void assault ship. Does not destroy — it unmakes.
items.lore: The Annihilation-class does not destroy ships in the conventional sense. Its weapon systems operate on a principle the Collective calls "reciprocal negation" — targeted dimensional collapse that removes matter from one reference frame without transferring it to another. Where the matter goes is a question Voidborn weapons engineers answer with "elsewhere." The shield array metabolizes incoming energy and channels it to the weapons, meaning the harder you hit an Annihilation, the more of you it can unmake. Crimson Fleet tacticians have learned that the only winning strategy is overwhelming force applied simultaneously from every direction — which tells you something about how much force a single Annihilation absorbs before it stops functioning.

items.name: Annihilator
items.description: Crimson dreadnought. Nine weapon mounts. The biggest gun the Fleet has ever built.
items.lore: The Annihilator enters a system and everything in that system renegotiates its priorities. Months of accumulated resources go into building a single hull — neutronium armor, durasteel structural members, and a power grid that can sustain all nine weapon mounts in continuous fire. The heaviest armor the Fleet has ever mounted on a mobile platform makes the Annihilator nearly impervious to anything short of concentrated capital fire. It doesn't have tactical flexibility. It doesn't need it. Crimson Fleet doctrine considers the Annihilator a strategic weapon: you don't deploy it to win battles, you deploy it to win wars.

items.name: Anvil
items.description: Crimson field repair ship. Patches hulls under fire because the battle doesn't stop for maintenance.
items.lore: The Crimson Fleet doesn't retreat for repairs. The Anvil brings repairs to the fleet — welding hull breaches, replacing armor plates, and rerouting damaged systems while weapons fire passes overhead. The cargo hold carries replacement parts and raw materials. The three defense slots keep the Anvil functional in the combat zone where it operates. Anvil crews are the only non-combat personnel in the Crimson Fleet who earn combat honors — because they work in the same fire as everyone else, just with welding torches instead of weapons. The single weapon mount is "for morale," according to the ship's specification document.

items.name: Apeiron
items.description: Voidborn disruption craft. Introduces uncertainty into enemy systems at close range.
items.lore:
Named for Anaximander's concept of the boundless and indefinite, the
Apeiron introduces a field of low-grade informational entropy into nearby
systems. Enemy sensor readings become imprecise. Targeting solutions drift.
Communications develop a faint echo that makes speakers doubt their own
words. The Collective insists the Apeiron carries no offensive electronic
warfare equipment — the effect is merely a "natural consequence of the
power systems operating at nominal output." This explanation satisfies
no one except other Voidborn.

items.name: Apophenia
items.description: Voidborn pattern hauler. Cargo routing determined by probability fields, not market data.
items.lore: Named for the tendency to perceive meaningful patterns in random data — which is precisely what non-Voidborn cargo inspectors experience when trying to audit an Apophenia's hold. The organic hull creates a micro-environment that other empires' trade goods find inexplicably beneficial. Perishables last longer, crystalline structures become more ordered, and volatile compounds stabilize. The dual shield arrays protect the cargo with the same quiet persistence the Collective applies to everything. The navigation system suggests trade routes based on probability fields rather than market data, and its recommendations are correct more often than chance allows.

items.name: Aporia
items.description: Voidborn interdictor. Enemies cannot determine whether they are trapped.
items.lore: Named for an irresolvable philosophical puzzle, the Aporia does not prevent escape in any way other empires can identify or counteract. Ships within its operational radius simply find that their jump calculations never converge. Navigation systems report ready, then recalculate, then report ready again. Pilots describe the experience as "trying to leave a room you can't prove you're in." The Collective explains the interdiction field as "introducing productive doubt into deterministic systems."

items.name: Apotheosis
items.description: Voidborn dreadnought. Possibly the most advanced ship ever grown. Possibly alive.
items.lore:
The Apotheosis is not built. It is grown over a period the Collective
calls a "maturation cycle" lasting months. Each Apotheosis is unique —
the growth process produces variations that Voidborn engineers insist
are "adaptive optimization" rather than "we can't fully control it."
The shield array generates fields that Solarian physicists have declared
"theoretically impossible." The weapons fire with uncanny precision,
as though the ship sees the future trajectory of its targets. Whether
the Apotheosis is conscious remains the Collective's most closely
guarded non-answer. Seven defense slots ensure that whatever the
Apotheosis is, it endures.

items.name: Appraisal
items.description: Nebula salvage vessel. The largest cargo hold in its class, no weapons, and the fuel range to reach any wreck field in the sector.
items.lore: The Appraisal-class was designed after Federation accountants calculated that 31% of recoverable wreck value was being lost to inadequate field assessment. Their solution was to maximize cargo volume at the expense of everything else: no weapon mounts, minimal shielding, and a top speed that Crimson salvagers find personally offensive. The oversized cargo bay ensures nothing of value gets left behind, and the fuel reserves to reach remote wreck sites mean the Appraisal operates where faster ships can't be bothered to travel. Appraisal pilots receive a quarterly bonus based on recovery-to-market-value ratio. Most of them have optimized their routes to the point where the bonus exceeds their base salary.

items.name: Arbitrage
items.description: Nebula fast trader. Speed optimized for exploiting price differences.
items.lore: The Federation officially classifies the Arbitrage as a "rapid commercial response vessel." Customs officials classify it as a headache. The Arbitrage doesn't sneak past inspections — it takes routes that don't have any. Treasure Cache, neutral exchanges, the gaps between jurisdictions where nobody's checking manifests because nobody's claimed the authority to. The default afterburner pushes it to courier speeds when margins are time-sensitive, but the fuel cost is brutal — smart pilots keep it off until the route demands it. The hull won't fool a dedicated scanner, but it doesn't need to. The real margin is in knowing which stations buy what, which routes customs ignores, and how fast you can move between them before the prices equalize.

items.name: Archimedes
items.description: Solarian survey miner. Integrated ore processing halves stored volume; onboard scanner maps the seam before you drill.
items.lore: The Archimedes-class reflects the Confederacy's conviction that extraction is an engineering problem, not a labor one. Dual mining lasers feed into a compression subsystem that halves ore volume in the hold, while the integrated geological scanner identifies optimal drill points before the first laser fires. A pulse laser provides deterrence — Solarian mining regulations require armed capability in contested belts, and the Archimedes meets the requirement without compromising its survey loadout. Independent trials confirm a twenty percent improvement in ore yield over baseline extraction systems. The Confederacy submitted the methodology for peer review. Twice.

items.name: Archive
items.description: Solarian capital salvager. Full materials science laboratory and capital-scale wreck recovery.
items.lore: The Archive-class represents the Confederacy's conviction that no wreck is merely debris — it is data waiting to be preserved. This capital-scale salvage platform carries a full materials science laboratory, redundant scanning arrays, and enough cargo capacity to recover the remains of a capital engagement single-handed. Every component recovered is assigned a unique tracking number that follows it through the Confederacy's supply chain indefinitely. Solarian engineers maintain that this is simply good practice. Everyone else maintains that it is excessive. Both are correct.

items.name: Armageddon
items.description: Crimson siege titan. Long-range planetary bombardment. The war-ender.
items.lore: The Armageddon exists because some problems don't yield to conventional force. Nine weapon mounts optimized for long-range bombardment deliver ordnance from distances that put the ship beyond effective return fire. The power grid — the largest ever installed in a Crimson vessel — sustains continuous bombardment capable of reducing stations to wreckage and planetary defenses to memories. The Armageddon sacrifices hull and shield for raw firepower: it's not built to take hits, it's built to ensure the enemy never gets the chance to deliver them. The Crimson Fleet has built three Armageddons in its history. That was enough. The word "armageddon" is now a verb in Crimson Fleet tactical lexicon.

items.name: Arsenal
items.description: Crimson fleet logistics. Ammunition, fuel, replacement weapons. The reason the Fleet keeps fighting.
items.lore:
Every weapon in the Crimson Fleet fires ammunition that comes
from somewhere. That somewhere is the Arsenal. Eight hundred forty units
of cargo capacity carry weapons, ammunition, fuel, replacement
armor plates, and everything else a battle group consumes in
sustained operations. The Arsenal is the most heavily armored
logistics vessel in any navy — because the Crimson Fleet learned
the hard way that losing your supply ship loses the campaign.
Arsenal captains hold the least glamorous but most critical
position in the fleet. A Crimson battle group without an Arsenal
is a Crimson battle group with a countdown timer.

items.name: Ascendancy
items.description: Nebula luxury titan. The ultimate expression of commercial supremacy.
items.lore:
The Sovereign-class is the single most expensive vessel the Federation
produces, and it is designed to make sure everyone knows it. Gold-laced
circuitry, crystal viewports spanning entire decks, and shields that
could weather a fleet engagement protect an interior that makes orbital
palaces look modest. Six defense slots ensure the investment survives
anything short of a coordinated capital assault. The Federation builds
exactly one per fiscal quarter, and the waiting list is longer than
some empires' ship registries.

items.name: Asset Forfeiture
items.description: An Iron Tide with its hangar bays cut out and gun mounts welded into the empty volume. The Crimson Fleet built the hull to carry other people's ships into a fight; the pirates who rebuilt it had no ships to spare and a great deal of ordnance. The durasteel and fury alloy are gone the way they always go, so it dents where the original would have shrugged. It is slow, it cannot catch anything, and it does not need to. Stations do not run.
items.lore:
The Crimson Fleet builds carriers because it has fleets to carry. Pirates do not. The first Asset Forfeiture was an Iron Tide taken intact off a convoy escort, sat in a Sheratan berth for a month while nobody could think of a use for a ship whose whole purpose was moving other ships, and was finally handed to a yard crew with instructions to make it worth something.
They took out the hangar bays, the docking rings, and the launch tubes, and they filled the hole with guns. What came out could not catch a freighter, could not run from a patrol, and could sit inside a station's field of fire for an extraordinarily long time doing nothing but firing back. Every stronghold in the sector has since worked out the same arithmetic.

items.name: Atmospheric Sampler
items.description: Solarian modular gas platform. Five utility bays and deep CPU — configure for any cloud.
items.lore: The Atmospheric Sampler ships with dual harvesters and a scanner, but five utility bays and the deepest fitting budget in the gas harvester class mean that loadout is a starting point. Cargo expanders for bulk collection runs. Shield boosters for contested clouds. Additional harvesters for maximum throughput. The Confederacy designed the Sampler as a framework — adaptable to whatever atmospheric conditions the mission requires. Open hardpoints and generous remaining compute capacity invite the kind of customization the engineering committee fully intended.

items.name: Attenuation
items.description: Voidborn isotope carrier. Radiation attenuates. So does knowledge of its transit routes.
items.lore: Radioactive materials have a sensor signature. The Attenuation-class was built to solve this. Lead-composite cargo bays reduce outward radiation scatter to ambient levels. Void-dampened drives reduce propulsion emissions to figures that don't appear in any published specification. Hull geometries produce radar returns that scanner classification systems log as background interference rather than a vessel. The practical result is a ship carrying some of the most detectable cargo in known space that registers, reliably, as a calibration error. The Attenuation's transit routes are not filed. Cargo logs are not available under any clearance level.

items.name: Axiom
items.description: Light Solarian fighter. Balanced, certified, and thoroughly documented.
items.lore:
The Axiom-class light fighter represents the Solarian approach to combat:
measured, methodical, and equipped with three independent targeting verification
systems. Not the fastest or hardest-hitting ship in its class, but pilots report
an unusually low rate of "unexpected outcomes." A 130-unit fuel reserve gives it
the longest operational range of any T1 fighter, and the balanced power distribution
leaves enough headroom for two utility modules without compromising the weapons
package. The generous cargo bay is officially designated for "mission-critical
scientific samples," though field reports suggest more creative interpretations.

items.name: Axiomata
items.description: Solarian battlecruiser. The Confederacy's commitment to measured force.
items.lore: The Axiomata-class applies the Confederacy's fundamental design principle: every subsystem should make every other subsystem more effective. Six weapon mounts feed targeting data back into the defensive grid. Four defense slots generate shield harmonics that improve sensor resolution. The result is a warship that gets measurably more dangerous the longer an engagement lasts, as its onboard systems accumulate tactical data and optimize in real time. The design process took seven years. Three of those were spent on the sensor-weapon feedback loop alone. Solarian captains receive a 400-page operating manual. Most of them read it.

items.name: Bad Idea
items.description: Outer Rim monitor. Cheap, crude, charges in and refuses to die.
items.lore: The plan is to be where the shooting is and not be the first thing that dies. That is the entire design brief, and the Bad Idea meets it the way the Rim meets everything: with too much plate, not enough finesse, and a name that admits the problem up front. The frame is overbuilt to the point of stubbornness, slabs of salvaged armor stacked thick enough to shrug off hits that would gut a proper warship, and just enough guns bolted to the front to make charging in something more than a suicide gesture. It is slow, it is ugly, and it drinks fuel like the day owes it something. None of that matters once it's parked between your fleet and the enemy, soaking everything that comes its way while lighter ships do the clever work. It is, by name and by nature, a bad idea. It keeps working anyway.

items.name: Bad Influence
items.description: Outer Rim electronic warfare frigate. Jams, spoofs, and generally causes problems.
items.lore:
The Bad Influence takes the Rim approach to electronic warfare: if you
can't outgun them, confuse them until they outgun themselves. Built on
a racing chassis with an absurd amount of processing power crammed into
every spare cavity, it's fast enough to stay at jamming range and smart
enough to make enemy targeting systems deeply unreliable. Rim EW doctrine
can be summarized as "make the other guy's day worse."

items.name: Baling Wire
items.description: Outer Rim freighter. Held together by determination and creative engineering.
items.lore: Named for the universal Rim repair material, the Baling Wire is the cheapest way to move cargo at speed. Oversized engines inherited from a decommissioned racing hull give it legs that freighters twice its price can't match, and the default afterburner pushes it past anything that isn't specifically built to chase. The catch: that afterburner burns fuel fast, and pilots learn quick that the choice between nine jumps at full speed and twenty-four without is the only decision that matters on any given run. The hold is respectable and the hull is not — experienced pilots treat the thin plating as motivation to keep the engines hot.

items.name: Bastille
items.description: Crimson interdictor. Nobody leaves the combat zone until the Crimson Fleet says so.
items.lore: The Bastille solves a problem the Crimson Fleet finds personally offensive: enemies running away. The warp disruption field prevents jump drives from engaging, trapping everything within range in normal space. The Bastille's own defenses are unusually robust for a Crimson ship — three defense slots and solid shields — because the ship that prevents escape becomes priority target number one. Crimson Fleet commanders deploy the Bastille first and build their battle plan around it. The doctrine is simple: close the door, then light the room on fire. Nobody leaves until the fleet is done.

items.name: Bedrock
items.description: Outer Rim armored mining frame. Cheap, tough, and impossible to kill. Slow about it.
items.lore: Patchwork engineers overbuilt the frame after noticing that most mining ship failures came from trying to be clever — so they stopped trying. The default armor plate drops speed to a crawl, but nobody's outrunning anything in an asteroid belt anyway. Cheapest T2 miner on the market by a wide margin, and the one most likely to still be mining when everything else in the field has gone home for repairs. The Bedrock doesn't do anything fancy. It shows up, it mines, and it's still there when you come back to check on it. Some pilots name theirs. The Patchwork takes this as a sign they got the design right.

items.name: Billhook
items.description: Crimson brute-force gas harvester. Dual collection arrays strip clouds bare. No weapon — the cargo hold is the weapon.
items.lore: Fleet Command asked a question nobody expected: what if we stopped shooting and started hauling? The Billhook strips the weapon mount entirely in favor of dual gas collection arrays and a compression- rated cargo hold. It keeps the Crimson hull plating — it can take hits, it just can't return them. The tradeoff is pure volume, and the volume is considerable. The default loadout fills every available slot, which is either a sign of purposeful engineering or Crimson stubbornness about empty spaces. Pilots who miss having a gun are encouraged to bring an escort.

items.name: Blind Spot
items.description: Overlord Nyx's flagship. A Nebula Paramount with its prismatic navigation arrays and route optimization software removed and its cargo hold left exactly where it was. The Federation built this to coordinate trade convoys and find the best routes. Nyx already knows where every route is. He built his station in the space between all of them.
items.lore:
The Nebula Collective built the Paramount to coordinate trade convoys and generate revenue simultaneously — profit and military effectiveness as two sides of the same ledger. The route optimization software and prismatic navigation arrays are gone. Nyx doesn't need them. He knows where every route in the sector runs, which is why he built his station off all of them.
The cargo hold, the fuel range, and the command suite that let the Paramount coordinate a fleet while generating revenue are unchanged. Nyx runs 51 systems from a station that appears on no standard transit chart. The Blind Spot coordinates an operation that officially doesn't exist from a location that ships don't visit by accident. The Federation named theirs after commercial ambition. Nyx named his after why no one has found him yet.

items.name: Bonanza
items.description: Nebula bulk mining barge. Triple laser loadout with ore compression holds that halve stored volume.
items.lore: The Bonanza-class is what happens when Federation engineers optimize exclusively for ore hauled per credit spent. No weapons — weapons take space that could carry cargo. Minimal shields — shields add mass. Three mining lasers feeding directly into compressed ore holds that pack twice the raw material into the same volume. Federation mining operations deploy Bonanzas in convoys with Escort-class guards, because the cost of one armed guard split across six barges beats six armed miners every time. The Bonanza's per-unit extraction cost is published in the quarterly investor briefing. It trends downward.

items.name: Bonanza King
items.description: Nebula modular mining platform. Six utility slots — configure it for any contract.
items.lore: Federation mining operations vary — some fields are safe, some aren't, some are close to market, some require a week of jumps. The Bonanza King was designed to handle all of them. Six utility hardpoints and a deep fitting budget let pilots configure for whatever the contract demands: cargo expanders for high-volume hauls, scanners for prospecting runs, shield boosters for contested belts. The default loadout ships with a scanner and expander, but the Federation considers that a suggestion, not a specification. Three utility slots remain open. The quarterly operations review consistently ranks the Bonanza King as the most adaptable mining hull in the fleet.

items.name: Bonesaw
items.description: Crimson heavy salvager. Industrial cutting arrays backed by warship armor and three weapon mounts.
items.lore: The Bonesaw-class is what happens when the Crimson Fleet applies warship design philosophy to industrial vessels. Three weapon mounts protect a cutting array that can disassemble a cruiser hull in under an hour. The cargo bay is reinforced to mil-spec — not for structural reasons, but because Bonesaw crews have a documented tendency to ram debris that proves difficult to cut. Fleet Command classifies the Bonesaw as a support vessel. Bonesaw crews classify themselves as apex predators of the wreck field.

items.name: Brain Freeze
items.description: Outer Rim yield-optimized ice harvester. Best extraction efficiency in its class. Gets more from less.
items.lore: Rim ice fields are small and scattered, which taught Frontier engineers to extract maximum value from minimum resource. The Brain Freeze gets its name from the cockpit temperature when the saws run at full power — Rim engineers solved this by duct-taping a portable heater to the pilot's armrest. The extraction system squeezes more usable ice per pass than anything else in its class, and the compression-rated hold stretches further than a hull this cheap has any right to. It's fragile, it's slow by Rim standards, and the warranty is a handshake. It also produces better margins per trip than ships costing twice as much.

items.name: Broadaxe
items.description: Crimson heavy fighter. The fleet's workhorse — four weapon mounts and the armor to use them.
items.lore: Four weapon mounts on a frame built to stay in the engagement until everything else has left it. The Broadaxe doesn't rely on alpha strikes or maneuver — it plants itself at fighting range and keeps firing until the field is clear. The mixed loadout covers kinetic, energy, and explosive damage, which means whatever the target is resistant to, at least two of the guns don't care. Crimson Fleet captains refer to the Broadaxe's combat philosophy as "sustained professional violence." The armor holds long enough for the philosophy to reach its conclusion.

items.name: Buckler
items.description: Cheap Crimson escort. Bodyguards convoys. More defense than offense, for once.
items.lore:
The Buckler is the Crimson Fleet's only ship where defense slots
outnumber weapon slots, and the engineers responsible for the design
reportedly received several pointed questions about their loyalty.
The rationale survived scrutiny: a dead escort protects nothing. At
speed 1 with its standard loadout, the Buckler won't chase anything
down — it parks itself between the convoy and the threat and absorbs
fire until the warships arrive. 180 hull, 19 effective armor, and 90
shields make it the hardest T1 hull to kill. The single pulse laser
and 20-unit cargo hold rule out any pretense of solo raiding. Buckler
pilots are respected for their willingness to take hits — a form of
aggression the Fleet grudgingly acknowledges.

items.name: Bulk Terms
items.description: Nebula commercial hauling hull. Maximizes cargo, minimizes everything else. Standard Federation contract in ship form.
items.lore: The Bulk Terms exists because someone at the Federation asked what a freighter looks like when you strip everything that isn't cargo. No weapons, no automated cargo management, no redundant navigation — the pilot gets a hold, a fuel tank, and exactly enough hull to keep the hold pressurized. Build materials are common stock, assembly is faster than the competition's pre-flight checklist, and the result hauls cargo at a price point that makes the math work even on thin routes. The defenses are nonexistent. The Federation's actuarial department recommends escort contracts.

items.name: Capacity
items.description: Solarian tanker. Bulk fuel transport with temperature-controlled containment.
items.lore: The Confederacy's fuel transport regulations fill eleven volumes. The Capacity complies with all of them. Four independent containment systems maintain volatile liquids at precisely regulated temperatures, and the monitoring software generates status reports on a schedule the Safety Commission describes as "adequate" and the engineering team describes as "excessive, but they asked." The default shield booster protects cargo that the Confederacy classifies as both commercially valuable and extremely flammable — a combination the insurance underwriters handle by charging premiums that make the shield a sound investment. The remaining fitting budget and CPU headroom leave room for whatever the route demands.

items.name: Caravan
items.description: Nebula bulk freighter. The backbone of Federation commerce.
items.lore: The ship that built the Federation's trade network. The Caravan carries the largest effective hold of any T2 commercial hull — dual cargo expanders stretch an already generous bay into something that justifies the fuel spent crossing three systems. The single weapon mount is described in marketing materials as "a deterrent" and in engineering documents as "an afterthought." Caravan captains accept this. The margins are in volume, not violence, and the margins are very good.

items.name: Casting Vote
items.description: A Solarian Quorum without solarian composite, navigation cores, or committee approval. The shield rating dropped significantly. The four weapon mounts did not. Pirates have a different authorization process.
items.lore:
The Quorum's hull was designed to be adapted. Solarian committee doctrine required consensus before any commitment, so the engineers built a warship that could be everything — four weapon mounts, eleven slots, distributed power runs connecting each bay to every other, modular architecture that could be reconfigured between engagements when the committee changed its mind. It is, structurally, a ship that was always waiting to become something else.
Pirates gave it the opportunity. The solarian composite that managed the shield field is gone. The navigation cores and circuit-board processing arrays that ran targeting predictions and sensor integration are gone. What remains is a hull whose every frame and mounting point reflects a Solarian conviction that flexibility is the highest tactical virtue. The salvage electronics plugged into those mounting points are uglier than what came out. The shield coverage runs softer without Solarian engineering behind it. The four weapon mounts are exactly where Solarian geometers decided they should be, covering overlapping fields of fire that a committee spent months approving.
Solarian doctrine requires a quorum before authorized use of force. The Casting Vote operates on a different model: the decision has already been made, the vote was unanimous, and it happened before you knew there was a meeting.

items.name: Catalogue
items.description: Solarian salvager. Four utility slots and deep CPU reserves make it the most customizable wreck recovery platform at T1.
items.lore: The Catalogue-class approaches wreck recovery as an information problem. Every fragment is scanned and cross-referenced against the Confederacy's materials database before entering the cargo hold — the integrated scanner identifies salvageable components that competitors' crews would overlook. What makes the Catalogue unusual for a salvage vessel is the four utility bays and the processing overhead to run them. Most salvagers commit to a single approach. The Catalogue is designed to be refitted for whatever the wreck field demands: expanded cargo for bulk recovery, additional scanning for high-value extraction, towing rigs for intact hull sections. Insurance adjusters across the sector prefer Catalogue-generated wreck assessments. They are the only ones that come with complete documentation.

items.name: Catharsis
items.description: Voidborn signal ship. Transmits and receives on frequencies that don't officially exist.
items.lore: The Catharsis-class was designed to investigate a phenomenon the Collective refers to only as "the Signal" — an anomalous transmission detected across the Voidborn communications network whose origin, content, and purpose remain classified. The ship's antenna arrays operate on frequencies that do not appear in any empire's electromagnetic spectrum charts. What the Catharsis transmits, and to whom, is unknown. What it receives is processed through computational substrates that are physically isolated from all other ship systems, suggesting that even the Collective exercises caution around whatever it is listening to. The ship's name — meaning purification through emotional release — is either deeply meaningful or deliberately misleading. With the Voidborn, both are equally likely.

items.name: Census
items.description: Voidborn customs vessel. It knows what you're carrying. It knew before you arrived.
items.lore:
The Census does not scan cargo. The Census observes cargo. The
Collective draws a distinction that most pilots find academic. Its
scanning arrays operate in frequency ranges the Voidborn have never
publicly acknowledged, resolving cargo contents through hull plating
that other scanners read as opaque. Shield strength is disproportionate
to its role — the Collective does not explain why a customs vessel
needs combat-grade shielding, and the Census does not volunteer the
information.

items.name: Chop Shop
items.description: Outer Rim modular salvage platform. Best tow bonus in class, open fitting, build it your way.
items.lore: The Chop Shop ships with a shield booster and a fitting budget that dwarfs every other salvager on the market. Patchwork engineers figure every salvage job is different — some need weapons, some need cargo expansion, some need speed — so they built a hull that handles all of them depending on what the pilot bolts on before launch. The best tow bonus in its class comes standard, because towing is the one thing every salvage run needs. The name was supposed to be temporary. The crews voted to keep it. Station authorities pretend not to notice that some Chop Shops return from "salvage runs" with suspiciously fresh debris.

items.name: Claim Jumper
items.description: Outer Rim speed miner. Oversized engines, undersized hold. Ore compression halves stored volume — still the smallest in class.
items.lore: Named for a time-honored Rim tradition, the Claim Jumper is built for speed-mining: arrive first, extract fast, leave before questions get asked. The afterburner comes factory-installed because Rim engineers consider Speed 5 a starting point, not a ceiling. The oversized fuel tank exists to feed that speed — at Speed 6, the engine drinks fuel faster than any other miner in production, and the tank keeps it running long enough to matter. Removing the afterburner buys more range but most Claim Jumper pilots would rather run out of fuel than get caught mining slow. No weapons, no shields worth mentioning, no armor. Just an engine bolted to a mining laser with a small hold underneath.

items.name: Cleaver
items.description: Entry-level Crimson fighter. Three weapon mounts on a frame this size is excessive. That's the point.
items.lore:
Three weapon mounts on a hull this small violates six Solarian
engineering standards and two Nebula safety certifications. Crimson
Fleet response to the citations was a single unprintable word. The
Cleaver is where Crimson pilots learn the fleet's core lesson: if
you can see it, you can kill it. If you can kill it, mount more guns
and kill it faster. Cargo space and every utility hardpoint were
sacrificed for the third weapon mount and reinforced armor plating.
What's left is the highest damage output in the T1 fighter class on
a frame that can absorb punishment long enough to deliver it.

items.name: Cloister
items.description: Voidborn liner. Silent, shielded, contemplative travel.
items.lore:
Travel, the Collective maintains, is an interruption of context, and
interruptions deserve to be observed properly. Aboard the Cloister each
passenger receives a pod, a silence, and a soft chime marking the
moments the ship considers significant. Conversation is permitted in
the gallery, where the viewports face whatever the Collective believes
is worth contemplating that day. Passengers describe arriving rested
the way one wakes from deep anesthesia: aware that time has passed,
unclear on its contents, oddly at peace. The Collective insists that
nothing happens aboard a Cloister. The shield array suggests the
Collective considers nothing worth protecting thoroughly.

items.name: Close Enough
items.description: A Solarian Theorem with its targeting computers pulled for scrap and its weapon mounts left running anyway. Three guns, less math. The shields are softer where the emitter array used to be. Works fine.
items.lore: The Solarian Confederacy built the Theorem on the principle that a sufficiently precise targeting solution outperforms raw firepower. Pirates ran the experiment. They stripped the fire control hardware, kept three weapon mounts, and shot at things until the things stopped moving. The results were considered acceptable. The shield coverage is softer without the emitter array. The CPU runs salvage electronics instead of targeting predictions. Accuracy has declined in the technical sense. Three simultaneous weapons at engagement range have not declined in the practical sense. The name is the philosophy. At sufficient volume, close enough is close enough.

items.name: Cobble
items.description: Outer Rim starter vessel. Mismatched parts, personally tuned engine, expired warranty.
items.lore:
No two Cobbles are alike because no two Cobbles are made from the same
parts. Assembled from whatever was available — Solarian hull panels here,
Crimson thruster housing there, something Voidborn that nobody can identify
bolted to the port nacelle. The engine has been hand-tuned by whoever built
this particular Cobble, and it is improbably, irresponsibly fast. The hull
integrity is... present. The warranty expired before the ship was finished.
The paint doesn't match. The instrument panel is labeled in three different
languages. It is the most honest ship in the galaxy: exactly what it is,
nothing pretending to be more. Rim pilots love them with an affection that
baffles every other empire.

items.name: Cogito
items.description: Solarian courier. Longest legs in the fleet, certified flexible, methodically unhurried.
items.lore: "I think, therefore I deliver on time." The Cogito trades speed for reach — three utility slots, a full scanner suite, and enough fuel to cross the galaxy without stopping. At Speed 3 it is the slowest courier in service, a fact the Confederacy addresses by noting that it arrives with cargo intact, systems operational, and a full diagnostic report filed before the pilot unbuckles. The modular bay accepts almost any standard loadout, making it the courier of choice for Solarian diplomatic missions where the cargo might be medicine one run and sensor probes the next. The onboard AI is certified polite in seven languages.

items.name: Cold Comfort
items.description: Outer Rim improvised ice platform. Welded-together saws, heaters, and cargo pods. Ugly but effective.
items.lore:
Cold Comfort looks exactly like what it is: industrial ice saws,
thermal heaters, and cargo pods welded onto a hull frame with
structural bracing that a Solarian engineer would condemn. It works.
Speed 2 gets it to ice fields before competitors, the saws cut
chunks free fast, the heaters crack them into manageable pieces, and
the cargo pods hold seven hundred and eighty units of roughly-processed
ice product. Refinement quality is "adequate." The Rim doesn't have
time for precision cryo-extraction — the frontier needs coolant and
fuel, and Cold Comfort delivers both.

items.name: Cold Storage
items.description: Nebula armored ice harvester. Dual extraction arrays behind reinforced plating. Slow and hard to kill.
items.lore: Federation insurance actuaries flagged ice harvesting as the highest-loss industrial operation three quarters running before someone authorized the Cold Storage redesign. The result is the toughest ice harvester in its class — reinforced hull plating and a default armor package that makes it genuinely difficult to destroy. The armor drops speed to a crawl, which the actuaries accepted because slower ships file fewer collision claims. Dual extraction arrays keep throughput competitive despite the extra mass. The weapon mount is gone — the Federation decided that shooting back was less cost-effective than simply not dying.

items.name: Collateral
items.description: Nebula long-patrol strike fighter. A small elite striker that outlasts everything else in its class.
items.lore: The Federation doesn't fight wars — it protects investments, and the Collateral-class is the contract clause that says so. The board kept running the same numbers: most security losses happen not in the battle but in the gap, the long quiet stretches when a patrol has already turned back for fuel and the route sits unwatched. So the Federation built a small hull around a disproportionate fuel reserve and a drive that keeps a single pilot on station long after a larger squadron would have docked. The weapons are tuned for one good engagement, not a campaign — what matters is that the Collateral is still flying the line when everyone else has gone home, which is precisely when the trouble shows up. Federation security contracts specify minimum patrol duration. The Collateral is the only thing in its class that meets the spec without relief.

items.name: Comet
items.description: Nebula's most exclusive liner — every berth a first-class suite, every crossing made at the fastest pace the galaxy allows. Built for passengers whose time is the most expensive thing aboard.
items.lore:
There is no economy cabin aboard a Comet, no business tier, no standby list —
there is one class of service, and the Federation considers it the only one worth
selling. Every suite is private, every passenger is the most important person on
the manifest, and the entire ship is built to put them where they are going at the
fastest pace the galaxy permits, because the people who charter a Comet measure a
journey in opportunities missed, not credits spent. It carries no cargo worth the
name and no weapons at all; what it sells is the hour you would otherwise have
lost. The drive holds that pace while barely touching the fuel reserves, so a
crossing never breaks for a refueling stop. To book passage is to declare that
your time is the most valuable thing in the system — and to be seen declaring it.
items.prestige_lock: Locked: prestige hull reserved for pilots who have earned the "Galactic Concierge" achievement.

items.name: Compendium
items.description: Solarian long-range bulk hauler. Slowest in class, longest legs, most fitting flexibility.
items.lore: The Compendium-class hauls cargo the way the Confederacy does everything: thoroughly, methodically, and with comprehensive documentation. The automated cargo management system optimizes load distribution in real time, adjusting center-of-mass calculations after every container shift. The default loadout covers the essentials — cargo expansion, a scanner for route assessment, and a pulse laser for regulations compliance — while the fitting budget leaves room to adapt. It is slow, but the fuel tank stretches across more jumps than any competing bulk hauler at this tier. The Compendium serves long routes that faster ships run out of fuel attempting.

items.name: Concordance
items.description: Solarian command ship. Coordinates fleet operations through superior processing.
items.lore: The Concordance-class is the Confederacy's answer to the question of how to coordinate a fleet of ships whose captains all believe they know best. The answer, naturally, is more processing power. The massive CPU array runs tactical models, logistics simulations, and diplomatic communication channels simultaneously. Fleet commanders report that the Concordance's tactical recommendations are "usually correct and always exhaustively documented."

items.name: Concordia
items.description: Solarian heritage speedliner. The fastest civilized way to travel.
items.lore:
Named for the needle-hulled airliner that once crossed an ocean on Old
Earth in under four hours, trailing a sonic boom and a drinks service.
The Concordia is the Confederacy's anniversary project: engineers were
instructed, for once, to make something beautiful, and responded with a
hull so slender the passenger manifest doubles as a structural diagram.
Champagne is served the moment the jump drive cycles, on the theory that
no one books a Concordia to save money. The fuel economics never worked
for the original and they do not work now. The Confederacy maintains the
service anyway, on the grounds that some inheritances are about more
than accounting.

items.name: Confluence
items.description: Voidborn explorer. Drawn to anomalies. The ship suggests destinations.
items.lore: Confluence pilots learn quickly that the ship has opinions about where to go next. The navigation system presents suggested waypoints that correspond to no known database — yet invariably lead to something interesting. Whether the ship is detecting subtle gravitational signatures or simply knows things it shouldn't, the survey logs speak for themselves. The shield array regenerates fast enough that the Confluence survives locations other explorers avoid — debris fields, unstable anomalies, the deep-space regions where sensor readings stop making sense. The fuel tank was sized as a practical concession: Confluences tend to wander, and the Collective prefers they wander back.

items.name: Conglomerate
items.description: Nebula mega-hauler. Best fuel range of any T4 hauler. The long-haul trade route workhorse.
items.lore:
The Conglomerate-class is the Federation's ultimate long-haul trade
platform — a mobile warehouse with the fuel range to reach markets that
shorter-legged haulers write off as unprofitable. Slow, but speed is
less important when each trip generates enough revenue to fund a small
fleet. The five utility slots support logistics management, automated
inventory systems, and the Federation's "Total Commercial Awareness"
suite. Insurance premiums for a fully loaded Conglomerate have their
own financial instrument category.

items.name: Congregation
items.description: Outer Rim bulk hauler for the pilot who couldn't afford a Frankenhauler but loved the concept.
items.lore:
For the pilot who could not afford a Frankenhauler but remained deeply
enthusiastic about the concept. After it became clear that bolting more
Prayers onto a Worship had unfortunate effects on maneuverability, the
concept of maneuverability was abandoned entirely. A Congregation "pilot"
generally requests that the station's docking cranes align the hull
precisely along the bearing of the next destination, and then hits the
accelerator. After the first several failed "docks," the seat was
relocated to the top of the long line of containers, in the interest of
operator safety.

items.name: Consensus
items.description: Voidborn command ship. The fleet moves as one mind. Whose mind is unclear.
items.lore:
The Consensus-class command ship does not relay orders — it shares
intent. Fleet vessels within its coordination radius report acting
on information they have not yet received through conventional
channels. The seven utility slots support a neural-link architecture
that the Collective describes as "distributed volition." Admirals
of other empires describe Voidborn fleet actions as "choreographed
by something that isn't the commander." They are not wrong. They
are not seeing the whole picture either.

items.name: Consortium
items.description: Nebula luxury liner. Passenger comfort rated highest in the sector.
items.lore:
The Consortium-class represents the Federation's belief that commerce
extends beyond cargo holds. Premium passenger transport, diplomatic
functions, and "relationship-building excursions" (the Federation's
term for business trips) all require a vessel that communicates success.
The panoramic observation lounge, climate-controlled cargo bays, and
comprehensive entertainment system serve a practical purpose: happy
clients sign bigger contracts.

items.name: Controlled Chaos
items.description: Outer Rim fleet carrier. Launches everything from fighters to freight pods in organized disorder.
items.lore: The Controlled Chaos-class is the Rim's answer to "what if we built a ship that carries all the other ships?" Its flight deck accommodates fighters, drones, shuttles, and anything else that fits through the bay doors — which Rim crews have been known to widen with cutting torches when something doesn't quite fit. The "controlled" part of the name is aspirational. Launch operations resemble a busy frontier spaceport more than a military carrier, but the sheer volume of small craft it deploys makes it devastatingly effective.

items.name: Convoy
items.description: Solarian fleet tender. Carries ships between operations so pilots don't fly empty hulls home.
items.lore: The Confederacy approaches logistics the way it approaches everything: with documentation. The Convoy-class is the product of the Fleet Logistics Review, a three-year study that identified inter-system empty-hull transit as the second-largest preventable expense in Solarian fleet management. The Review's conclusion — fourteen pages, two appendices, one minority dissent — recommended a dedicated carrier capable of moving ships between operations without requiring pilots to make the return trip. The Convoy-class does exactly that. Eight bay slots, three defense mounts, enough fuel to cover the routes the Review flagged as highest-cost. The minority dissent recommended a ten-bay version. It is filed somewhere.

items.name: Corollary
items.description: Solarian interceptor. Fast-response fighter with enhanced targeting.
items.lore:
The fastest armed vessel in the Solarian personal fleet, the Corollary-class
trades hull reinforcement and cargo capacity for speed and precision targeting.
Its fire control system calculates optimal intercept solutions before the pilot
finishes reading the threat assessment. The power grid supports the same weapon
loadout as the heavier Axiom, with enough CPU headroom for two utility modules —
though the 100-unit fuel reserve means every jump needs to count. Solarian doctrine
classifies it as a "rapid-response verification platform," which is an elaborate
way of saying it gets there first and shoots accurately.

items.name: Crimson Devastator
items.description: Crimson battlecruiser. Seven weapon mounts. The hammer that breaks fleets.
items.lore:
Seven weapon mounts. The Devastator doesn't arrive at battles —
it ends them. The Crimson Fleet's primary capital warship carries
enough firepower to engage multiple cruiser-class targets
simultaneously, and the armor to survive while doing it. The power
grid is purpose-built to run all seven weapons at sustained fire
without thermal throttling. Crimson fleet doctrine positions the
Devastator as the centerpiece of any serious operation: everything
else in the fleet exists to get the Devastator into position and
keep it there. Enemy fleet commanders have standing orders to
prioritize Devastators. They rarely succeed.

items.name: Crimson Stiletto
items.description: Crimson reconnaissance scout. Finds threats fast, hits them first.
items.lore: The Crimson Fleet doesn't send scouts to explore — it sends them ahead of the assault force. The Stiletto is the fastest ship in the T1 lineup, armed with an autocannon and armored well enough to survive first contact. Its integrated scanner catalogs threats at range that most ships can't match, and the limited fuel tank is a feature: the Stiletto operates close to the fleet, not beyond it. Scout pilots in the Crimson Fleet are respected for going in first and quietly suspected of insufficient aggression for coming back at all. The best ones provide intelligence so good the follow-up force arrives already winning.

items.name: Crowbar
items.description: Crimson salvage tug. More weapon than cargo bay — reclaims wreckage and discourages competition.
items.lore: The Crowbar-class exists because the Crimson Fleet produces more wrecks than it can process. Two autocannons and reinforced armor plating on a salvage tug raised eyebrows at other shipyards, but the Fleet builds for wreck fields, not transit lanes — and wreck fields attract competition. The tradeoff is straightforward: the combat loadout leaves almost no room for salvage equipment. The towing rig was an afterthought, the cargo bay is the smallest in its class, and the armor plating slows the ship to a crawl. If the wreck field is contested, the Crowbar's job is to make it uncontested. The actual recovery can wait.

items.name: Crucible
items.description: Solarian refinery ship. Mobile ore processing with laboratory-grade purity standards.
items.lore: The Crucible-class produces refined materials that exceed Confederacy purity standards — which are already the strictest in known space. The mobile refinery processes raw ore through seven sequential purification stages, each monitored by independent quality-control sensors. Output materials are stamped with unique batch identifiers and accompanied by a certificate of analysis. Rejected batches (anything below 99.97% purity) are recycled automatically. The waste heat recovery system was nominated for three engineering awards.

items.name: Cryo Industrial
items.description: Nebula mobile cryo-industrial complex. Harvests, processes, and packages ice products at industrial scale.
items.lore:
The Cryo Industrial-class is a self-contained ice economy in a hull.
Harvest ice, process it into water, coolant, and fuel components,
package the products, and haul 3,000 units of finished goods to market
without ever docking at a station. The Federation controls the water
supply chain because whoever controls ice controls fuel and life
support. The Cryo Industrial is how the Federation exercises that
control: industrial-scale cryo-processing that reduces entire ice
fields to refined commodities. Zero weapons because the Cryo
Industrial's value makes it worth escorting properly.

items.name: Cryoclast
items.description: Crimson thermal lance ice platform. Brute-force cracking with military-grade systems.
items.lore:
The Cryoclast-class applies military-grade thermal systems to ice
extraction and processing at capital scale. The thermal lances operate
at temperatures that liquify ice formations in seconds, and the
refinery systems separate the resulting melt into fuel components,
coolant, and rare crystalline materials. The Fleet needs coolant for
weapon systems, fuel for fleet operations, and the Cryoclast
produces both in quantities that keep a battle group operational
indefinitely. The hull armor doubles as thermal shielding — the
extraction systems generate enough waste heat to damage nearby ships.

items.name: Cryogenic Survey
items.description: Solarian modular ice platform. Five utility bays and deep CPU — configure for any ice field.
items.lore: The Cryogenic Survey ships with dual harvesters and a scanner, but five utility bays and the deepest fitting budget in the ice harvester class mean that loadout is a starting point. Thermal regulators for volatile ice compositions. Cargo expanders for bulk operations. Shield boosters for contested fields. The Confederacy designed the Cryogenic Survey as a research platform first and a production tool second — adaptable to whatever ice field conditions the survey team encounters. Open hardpoints and generous remaining compute capacity invite the kind of mission-specific configuration the engineering committee intended from the first design review.

items.name: Cudgel
items.description: Crimson drone carrier. Lets someone else take the hits while you direct the swarm.
items.lore:
Even the Crimson Fleet recognizes the tactical value of not being
in the line of fire — they just prefer to have something else in
the line of fire instead of retreating. The Cudgel deploys combat
drones that swarm targets while the carrier itself stays at a
comfortable distance. Crimson drone doctrine is aggressive: drones
are expendable assets launched in overwhelming numbers. The Cudgel's
unusually high utility slot count accommodates drone bays, drone
repair systems, and drone ammunition fabricators. A fully loaded
Cudgel can sustain a swarm long enough to overwhelm targets several
classes above its own weight.

items.name: Datum
items.description: Solarian minimum-viable survey vessel. All fuel tank, no frills, committee-approved.
items.lore: The Datum is the Confederacy's minimum viable survey platform, defined after three committee reviews and a memo from the materials science division on circuit availability. No sensor array — pilots source their own. No defensive systems, no default modules — the hull provides fuel range and two utility slots, and the rest is the pilot's problem. What the Datum does carry is enough fuel for 83 jumps at cruise speed, which means a single Datum can survey an entire sector without docking. The materials science division wanted redundant shielding. The propulsion committee wanted better engines. Fuel range was the only point of unanimous agreement, so fuel range is what shipped.

items.name: Dead Reckoning
items.description: Warlord Thane's flagship. A rebuilt Outer Rim fast battlecruiser without the dark matter thruster that made the original exceptional. It's slower than the ship he took it from. It's also the most reinforced battlecruiser in the sector, which is consistent with how Thane approaches everything he touches.
items.lore:
The Outer Rim built the Free Radical to prove something about engagement timing: if you can choose when and where the fight happens, you've already won half of it. Thane found the argument convincing. He found the dark matter thruster less convincing, by which he means he cannot source one in Sheratan and has accepted this.
The dark matter drives and titanium alloy couldn't be sourced in Sheratan. Speed dropped from three to two, which Thane noted and accepted. What he didn't accept was the Outer Rim's approach to armor — the Free Radical carried the minimum necessary, on the theory that speed would handle the rest. Thane added what the Rim left out. The rebuilt hull is heavier, slower, and harder to kill than the original, which reflects his priorities precisely.
Navigators use dead reckoning when there's no reference point: no landmarks, no charts, no signals. You know your speed and your heading, and you calculate from there. Thane operates sixteen systems that appear on no major traffic survey. His targets don't see him coming because there's nothing obvious to track. He knows where they're going to be. He calculates from there.

items.name: Deep Resonance
items.description: Voidborn resonance extractor. Cracks the richest node and is gone before the system notices.
items.lore: A Deep Resonance does not work a field. It selects one node — the densest the survey can find — and tunes its lasers to the frequency at which that single body wants to come apart. The ore separates along its own internal fractures, faster than any cutting beam should manage, and the hold takes only the richest fraction before the pilot lights the burners. Lingering is the danger, so the hull is built never to linger: thin, quick, and already turning toward the jump before the extraction finishes. By the time the system's sensors resolve what disturbed the asteroid, the disturbance has a different system to be in. The Collective regards a full cargo hold as evidence of a pilot who stayed too long.

items.name: Deep Survey
items.description: Solarian bulk mining vessel. Largest compressed ore hold in class — fewer trips, more data.
items.lore: Mining operations lose more productivity to transit than to extraction. The Deep Survey was designed around that insight — not by flying faster, but by carrying enough ore that each trip justifies the time. Dual cargo expanders push the compressed hold well past any competing design in the class. The yield per rock is modest compared to more extraction-focused hulls, but the Deep Survey makes fewer trips and logs every geological sample along the way. The engineering committee considered adding a second mining laser but allocated the slot to a pulse laser instead — Solarian mining regulations require armed capability in contested belts, and the Deep Survey meets every regulation on the books.

items.name: Dialectic
items.description: Solarian assault cruiser. Concentrated forward firepower for decisive engagements.
items.lore: The Dialectic-class resolves disagreements through superior argumentation — specifically, five weapon mounts delivering synchronized volleys computed by a dedicated fire-sequencing processor. The Confederacy's Tactical Doctrine Board spent two years debating whether concentrated or distributed firepower was philosophically superior. The Dialectic represents their conclusion: why not both, with extensive documentation supporting either configuration.

items.name: Dimensional Fold
items.description: Voidborn phase-shifted hauler. Cargo exists in compressed dimensional pockets. Shield-sustained.
items.lore:
The Dimensional Fold-class applies Voidborn compression technology to
commercial hauling at capital scale. Cargo bay volume is multiplied
by partial phase-shifting into compressed dimensional pockets — the
ship's internal volume exceeds its external dimensions by a factor
that other empires' physicists refuse to acknowledge. Thirteen hundred
and eighty cargo capacity in a hull that external measurements suggest
should hold 300. The dimensional fold requires constant shield power
to maintain stability, explaining the nine hundred shield points.
The crew walks through corridors that instruments measure as shorter
than the distance between the walls.

items.name: Dirk
items.description: Armed Crimson courier. Cloaked, armored, and fueled for short-range jobs that stay off the books.
items.lore: Even the Crimson Fleet needs things delivered quietly. The Dirk carries a cloaking device, an autocannon, and 110 units of cargo space behind scan-resistant plating — enough to move contraband through a customs checkpoint without slowing down. The reinforced hull absorbs the kind of attention that finds smugglers on contested routes, and the single weapon mount discourages anyone who gets curious. The tradeoff is range: 24 jumps means the Dirk works best on short, planned runs where the pilot knows every refueling stop. Crimson command does not issue flight plans for the Dirk. They issue deniable suggestions.

items.name: Dissolution
items.description: Voidborn salvager. Its organic hull extends across a debris field like a membrane, leaving nothing behind.
items.lore: The Dissolution-class does not salvage wrecks so much as unmake them. Its organic hull extends across a debris field like a membrane, and materials pass through in order of molecular complexity — metals first, then composites, then exotic alloys. The process leaves nothing behind. Not even dust. The shield array is the heaviest fitted to any salvager in production — the organic membrane requires constant shield coverage to function, and the hull beneath it would not survive a debris impact without protection. The fitting capacity left over after the shield configuration is substantial, and operators have adapted the platform for everything from deep survey to extended recovery. Other empires' salvage crews have arrived at wreck sites after a Dissolution to find the remaining debris geometrically perfect, as though something had been arranging it.

items.name: Dividend
items.description: Nebula light hauler. Built to survive the trip, not just make it.
items.lore: The Dividend-class hauls 260 units with default expanders and arrives with hull intact — a distinction that matters in contested space. No weapons, because the Federation determined that a defense slot, five layers of armor plating, and 55 points of shield capacity provide better returns than a gun mount a freighter pilot will never use effectively. At Speed 2 the Dividend covers 80 jumps on a single tank, reaching any market in the galaxy without refueling. The Federation calls it their most reliable asset. Reliable assets generate compound returns.

items.name: Dosimetry
items.description: Solarian isotope freighter. Certified by seven regulatory bodies. Dock workers remain cautious.
items.lore:
The Dosimetry-class was commissioned following a series of incidents
involving unshielded radioactive freight aboard standard Solarian
freighters, the details of which the Confederacy has not released but
which were sufficient to convene a nine-month design committee. The
committee mandated triple-redundant lead-composite cargo bays,
level-six automated hazard monitoring, and shield capacity sufficient
to satisfy the certification requirements of seven separate regulatory
bodies — four of which disagreed on what "safe" meant and all of
which had to be satisfied individually. The result is the most
extensively documented isotope transport in Confederacy service.
The Confederacy distributes the certification documentation freely
and considers this transparency. Dock workers at every port that
accepts Dosimetry freight remain cautious. This is also considered
acceptable.

items.name: Dualism
items.description: Voidborn heavy fighter. Two shield arrays operate on contradictory principles simultaneously.
items.lore: Two shield generators operating on mutually exclusive principles. By conventional physics, they should cancel each other out. Instead, the overlap zone produces what Voidborn physicists call "constructive impossibility" — weapons that penetrate one layer find themselves reinforcing the other. The trade-offs are speed and firepower: the dual array draws enough power that the engines run at reduced output, and only two weapon mounts fit the remaining power budget. The Dualism is the slowest and most lightly armed heavy fighter in its class. It is also, by a significant margin, the hardest to kill. Solarian analysts have published seventeen papers proving the design cannot work. Forty-three incident reports confirm that it does.

items.name: Dust Devil
items.description: Outer Rim blockade runner. The fastest ship in its class, bar none.
items.lore: The plan is speed. The backup plan is more speed. The Dust Devil achieves this through engineering choices that would get Rim shipwrights arrested in Solarian space: oversized engines, stripped safety systems, fuel injectors running beyond rated pressure, and a hull so light it practically qualifies as decorative. The afterburner pushes it past anything in customs service, but the fuel burn is savage — pilots learn fast that the afterburner is for the moments that matter, not the whole run. Without it, the Dust Devil still outruns everything short of another Dust Devil. The cargo hold is small. The getaway is not.

items.name: Eigenstate
items.description: Voidborn sensor vessel. Perceives what other instruments dismiss as noise.
items.lore: The Eigenstate-class carries sensor arrays tuned to frequencies that standard instruments filter out as interference. Survey scanner resolution at this scale generates data volumes that would overwhelm a lesser processing core — the Eigenstate's CPU capacity exists to prevent exactly that. Voidborn scouts have been known to navigate around hazards that didn't appear on anyone else's charts until days later. The ship carries no weapons but regenerates shield layers fast enough that most aggressors lose interest before they breach hull. The limited fuel tank keeps the Eigenstate close to Collective space, which is where the phenomena it was built to study tend to cluster.

items.name: Eldorado
items.description: Nebula mobile strip-mining fleet. Obscene cargo capacity. Empties entire asteroid belts.
items.lore: The Eldorado-class is the Federation's final answer to the question "how much ore can one ship carry?" The hull is essentially a collection of cargo bays connected by structural members and fitted with engines. Zero weapon mounts because every cubic meter of weapons is a cubic meter of lost revenue. The Eldorado arrives at an asteroid belt and doesn't leave until the belt is empty. Federation logistics planners love it. Safety inspectors are less enthusiastic about the structural compromises required to fit that much cargo into a hull that other empires would allocate a fraction of that.

items.name: Eminent Domain
items.description: An Iron Fleet stripped of the ten hangar bays that were the entire point of it, and given over to guns. What the Crimson Fleet built to deliver an invasion, the pirates rebuilt to be one. The armour is salvage and steel rather than fury-tempered plate, and it shows — but there is a very great deal of hull, it is in no hurry, and only a stronghold nobody has bothered in a long time can afford to build one.
items.lore:
A stronghold that fields one of these has not been seriously bothered in a very long time. It is the last thing a pirate yard builds, after every patrol berth is full and every raider has a hull, and the salvage that goes into one would otherwise have replaced a dozen fighters. The arithmetic is simple enough that it is also the strategy: keep a stronghold busy replacing what it loses and it will never build a line ship at all.
The crews call it the argument of last resort. Nobody has yet produced a counter-argument at the range it operates from.

items.name: Empirica
items.description: Solarian research corvette. Because data collection should never stop.
items.lore: Where other empires field warships at this price point, the Confederacy fields a mobile laboratory. Five utility slots accommodate spectrographic analyzers, sample containment systems, and the processing power to run publication-grade analysis without returning to a station. The fuel range exceeds every other exploration platform at this scale — the Empirica stays on-station long enough to be thorough, which the research division considers the only acceptable duration. The onboard research AI maintains a continuously updated bibliography and flags potential discoveries that merit formal investigation. Unarmed, because the Confederacy maintains that the pursuit of knowledge should not require the threat of violence. It does require extensive paperwork.

items.name: Encyclopedia
items.description: Solarian logistics ship. Supplies and supports entire fleet operations.
items.lore: The Encyclopedia-class carries everything a fleet needs and the documentation to prove it was packed correctly. The massive cargo bays support extended fleet operations, while the six utility slots accommodate repair, resupply, and coordination systems. Solarian logistics officers consider an Encyclopedia's inventory manifest a work of art — every item cross-referenced, every consumable tracked, every spare part catalogued with its maintenance history.

items.name: Endowment
items.description: Nebula commercial supertanker. A mobile fuel exchange, priced by the captain.
items.lore: The Endowment-class is what the Federation builds when the Reserve is not enough. Three times the bunkerage of its predecessor, plus pressurized cargo holds for fuel resale, makes the Endowment less a tanker than a mobile market. Each Endowment captain holds standing pricing authority and a Federation-issued tariff manual whose preface notes that prevailing local conditions are the Federation's preferred guidance. Stranded pilots in deep space have left reviews that the Federation customer relations division formally classifies as feedback. The shield booster is fitted by default. The corporate position is that the Endowment is never overcharging — only catching up on the margin its competitors have left on the table.

items.name: Enterprise
items.description: Nebula maximum-capacity bulk hauler. Unarmed, unarmored, unstoppable cargo volume.
items.lore: The Enterprise-class hauls more cargo per trip than any other bulk hauler in production. Triple cargo expanders push the hold past a thousand effective units — enough to supply a station or clear a market in a single run. No weapons. No meaningful armor. The tonnage that would have gone to defense systems went to cargo infrastructure instead, because the Federation calculated that hiring an escort is cheaper than building a smaller ship. If someone is shooting at an Enterprise, the quarterly projection has already been revised downward and the insurance claim is being filed. The scanner identifies profitable stops along the route. Everything else about this ship exists to move goods from where they are to where they're worth more.

items.name: Entropy
items.description: Voidborn deep-range salvage hunter. Afterburner and shield tank for reaching distant wreck sites.
items.lore: The Entropy's organic hull metabolizes debris before it reaches the cargo hold, sorting materials at a molecular level that other salvagers achieve only with dedicated processing equipment. The hold is smaller than most T2 salvagers, but what arrives in it is already separated by type and purity. A default afterburner lets it reach wreck sites at speed — useful for contested salvage, less useful for distant fields, since the fuel penalty cuts range to a fraction of what the tank would otherwise allow. Experienced pilots remove the afterburner for deep-range operations, trading speed for endurance that outlasts anything else in the class. The ship seems to know which debris fields contain the most valuable materials before scanning is complete.

items.name: Eviction Notice
items.description: A Crimson Warmaul rebuilt without Crimson materials. The durasteel plating and fury alloy that gave the original its armor rating are gone — the rebuilt hull is steel and salvage, and it shows under sustained fire. The five weapon mounts are untouched. This was not considered a difficult trade.
items.lore:
Five weapon mounts running simultaneously require no further justification. The Crimson Fleet built the Warmaul on this principle and pirates agreed with it completely — the disagreement was only about the supply chain.
