The fury alloy and durasteel are gone — the rebuilt hull takes hits harder. This has not changed how Crix runs the operation.
items.lore:
The Crimson Fleet uses the Overlord to coordinate battle groups because Crimson doctrine requires coordination to function — individual ships don't win engagements, formations do. Crix uses the Standing Order for the same reason, which puts him in unusual company for a pirate warlord.
The drone command module and sensor cluster couldn't be sourced. The fury alloy and siege plating are gone; the hull takes hits harder for it. The command suite is intact, running fleet-wide targeting, formation management, and coordinated fire concentration on salvage electronics — slightly less precisely and substantially more paranoidly, which Crix has found to be an improvement.
The Crix Stronghold station has a layout. This is noted because pirate stations generally don't. The Standing Order is the reason the station has one: when the flagship issues a formation order, the operation needs to be configured to receive it.

items.name: Start Praying
items.description: Cargo containers welded to an engine with a gun also welded to the engine. Pilot straps in outside, next to the gun. The Outer Rim said it cannot be armed. Pirates considered this a reasonable starting point.
items.lore:
The Prayer-class documentation stated clearly: no weapon mount, no defense system, no module slot of any kind. Pirates read this as a list of things to fix. The gun is real. The power draw for it is real. Whether 14 power units running a weapon mount on a ship with 40 hull points and an exposed pilot constitutes an improvement is a philosophical question the original designers did not anticipate being asked.
500 units of cargo capacity. The gun took the other forty. The pilot still wears a spacesuit and holds on, now next to an autocannon with a jury-rigged trigger cable running to the cockpit area, which remains absent. Named for what you do when you pull the trigger and realize you've made everything worse.

items.name: Stockade
items.description: Crimson bastion. Carries no guns and never will — it exists to be the thing the enemy shoots while the real warships do the killing.
items.lore: The Stockade has no weapon mounts. This is not an oversight the Fleet plans to correct. It is a slab of plating wrapped around enough reinforcement to keep that plating in one piece, and its only job is to stand where the enemy is shooting and keep standing. The doctrine writes itself: put the Stockade between the guns and the gunships, and let the enemy spend its volleys cracking armor that does not shoot back instead of killing the hulls that do. Every salvo the Stockade soaks is a salvo the warships behind it never feel, and that bargain — a dumb wall traded for a working battle line — is one the Fleet makes gladly. Crews assigned to it learn to take a particular pride in the arithmetic: the Stockade cannot win a fight, but it can decide one, simply by being the wrong thing to shoot at the right time. It will not kill you. It will make sure the ship that does kill you lives long enough to.

items.name: Subjugator
items.description: Crimson carrier titan. Deploys overwhelming drone swarms backed by capital-grade weapons.
items.lore: The Subjugator deploys drone swarms large enough to darken sensors. Where the Cudgel manages a small swarm and the Executioner combines drones with boarding, the Subjugator commits fully to the carrier doctrine: five dedicated weapon mounts for self-defense, six utility slots for drone bays and drone support systems, and the cargo capacity to carry replacement drones measured in the hundreds. A fully loaded Subjugator can sustain drone operations indefinitely, manufacturing replacement units from raw materials in the cargo hold. The swarm doesn't stop until the Subjugator runs out of metal.

items.name: Sublimation
items.description: Voidborn refinery ship. Raw materials transform in ways metallurgists cannot replicate.
items.lore: Named for the phase transition from solid directly to gas, the Sublimation-class refinery processes raw ore through biological catalysts that other empires cannot synthesize. Metals emerge from the refining chambers with crystal structures that should require pressures found only in stellar cores. The Collective's materials scientists describe the process as "persuading matter to remember what it could be." Yield rates are consistently above theoretical maximums, which the Collective attributes to "cooperative thermodynamics."

items.name: Substrate
items.description: Voidborn dimensional processor. Harvests and refines exotic matter from dimensional fractures.
items.lore: The Substrate does not process conventional materials. It operates at the boundary between normal space and the dimensional fractures that Voidborn technology routinely exploits, extracting what the Collective calls "null matter" — a substance that exists in a superposition of states until deliberately collapsed into useful form. The extraction process requires computational resources that would power a small station, hence the enormous CPU allocation. Other empires have attempted to replicate the process. Their attempts produce either nothing or explosions. The Collective attributes both outcomes to "insufficient philosophical preparation."

items.name: Superposition
items.description: Voidborn drone carrier. Each drone exists in multiple tactical states until observed.
items.lore:
The Superposition-class carries drone swarms that behave according to
principles borrowed from quantum mechanics — or possibly the other way
around. Enemy targeting systems report individual drones occupying
multiple positions simultaneously, collapsing to a single location
only at the moment of weapons impact. The Collective's published
specifications list the drone count as "contextual." Fleet intelligence
analysts have noted that the number of drones observed is always
exactly sufficient for the tactical situation, never more, never fewer.

items.name: Survey Vessel
items.description: Nebula expedition vessel. Deep-space exploration with all the comforts of a corner office.
items.lore: Eighty-five jumps on a single fuel load. The Survey Vessel exists because the Federation asked a simple question: what if a wormhole dumps you on the wrong side of the galaxy? Every other explorer relies on there being a station within range. The Survey Vessel doesn't. The massive fuel reserves and expedition-grade cargo hold mean a Federation wormhole survey team can transit an unknown wormhole, catalog whatever's on the other side, fill the hold with samples and trade data, and fly home the long way if the wormhole collapses behind them. The comfortable crew quarters remain a practical decision — panic makes poor surveyors.

items.name: Sustenance
items.description: Solarian supertanker. Capital-scale fuel transport for fleets that operate beyond resupply.
items.lore: The Sustenance-class brings Confederacy fuel doctrine to capital scale. Twenty-two pressurized bunkerage cells, each independently monitored, hold enough fuel to keep a six-ship convoy in deep transit for the better part of a Solarian fiscal quarter. The Bureau of Logistics designed the manifest tracking system before the engineering team had finished the hull, and the engineering team had to retrofit four additional sensor packages to satisfy reporting requirements they had not been told existed. The result is the most thoroughly documented tanker in the empire — every kilogram of fuel it carries is logged, signed, countersigned, and reconciled against three independent ledgers before it leaves the dock. Pilots note that the Sustenance is not fast, but it is consistent, a property the Confederacy considers more valuable than speed. The default damage control system reflects the Bureau's position that a tanker on fire is a regulatory matter best resolved before the regulators arrive.

items.name: Swarm Boss
items.description: Outer Rim light drone carrier. Launches salvaged drones at inconvenient velocities.
items.lore:
Rim drone engineering follows a simple principle: quantity has a quality
all its own. The Swarm Boss carries a complement of drones assembled from
whatever was cheap, available, and approximately the right shape. No two
drones are identical, their firmware is a patchwork of three different
operating systems, and their coordination protocols are best described as
"enthusiastic." What they lack in precision they make up for in numbers
and the sheer bewilderment they cause.

items.name: Syllogism
items.description: Solarian electronic warfare frigate. Disrupts enemy systems through superior processing.
items.lore:
The Syllogism-class proves that in modern space combat, the most dangerous
weapon is a sufficiently powerful processor running sufficiently clever
software. Solarian electronic warfare doctrine emphasizes "informational
superiority" — knowing exactly what the enemy is doing while ensuring they
know as little as possible about you. The massive CPU array supports
simultaneous jamming, spoofing, and real-time tactical analysis.

items.name: Symposium
items.description: Solarian command carrier. Fleet coordination through structured debate and evidence-based decision-making.
items.lore: A symposium is a gathering where ideas are debated and refined through structured discourse. The Symposium-class embodies this ideal: eight utility slots support drone bays, electronic warfare suites, fleet communication arrays, and repair systems. The processing core array — the most powerful ever installed on a mobile platform — simultaneously manages drone swarms, fleet tactics, and an automatic minutes-taking system that records every command decision for post-engagement review. Admirals must pass a written examination on committee governance procedures before assuming command. The examination has a 40% failure rate, which the Confederacy considers an appropriate filter.

items.name: Syndicate
items.description: Nebula speed trader. Half a freighter's hold on a hull fast enough to outrun the need for an escort.
items.lore: The Syndicate-class answers a question the Federation's actuaries kept circling back to: what does an escort contract actually buy? Protection, yes — but mostly it buys time, the hours a slow hull spends exposed on a contested route. The Syndicate buys those hours back another way. The hold is deliberately modest, sacrificed for a drive package and fuel reserves that let a captain pick a high-value cargo and simply be somewhere else before a raider can close the distance. The weapons are a courtesy to the optimist who tries anyway. Speed is the margin, and the margin pays for itself every time a Syndicate reaches the buy order while the convoy behind it is still negotiating with its escort.

items.name: Tariff
items.description: Nebula customs cruiser. The Federation's answer to every smuggler who thought scale-1 ships were the only thing watching the borders.
items.lore: The Tariff-class is what happens when the Federation decides that border security deserves capital-class investment. Three weapon mounts discourage resistance, heavy shields absorb the occasional disagreement, and the integrated scanner suite resolves cargo contents through military-grade hull plating at ranges that make jettisoning evidence impractical. The expanded cargo bay holds confiscated goods — the Federation does not waste seized merchandise, it redistributes it through official channels after a reasonable holding period and a modest handling charge. The name is deliberate — crossing Federation space without permission costs you one way or another.

items.name: Taxonomy
items.description: Solarian heavy salvager. Industrial-scale debris field processing with assembly-line material sorting.
items.lore: The Taxonomy-class processes entire debris fields with assembly-line precision — cataloguing, sorting, and storing recovered materials while the onboard laboratory identifies alloy compositions in real time. The default loadout covers the basics: a scanner for assessment, a cargo expander for volume, a pulse laser for cutting apart anything too large for the hold. What sets the Taxonomy apart is the fitting margin left over — the power grid and processing capacity accommodate substantially more equipment than the defaults consume, which means pilots refit for whatever the operation demands. Recovery reports from a Taxonomy operation have been accepted as evidence in three separate interstellar court proceedings.

items.name: Technically Legal
items.description: Outer Rim courier. Modified beyond manufacturer specs. Somehow still flies.
items.lore: Every component in a Technically Legal has been modified, bypassed, or replaced with something faster. The engine governor was removed and never reinstalled. The fuel injectors are from a ship two size classes larger, feeding a 200-unit tank that covers 50 jumps at cruising speed — or 33 at full afterburner, which is Speed 6, the fastest any courier moves at T1. The safety interlocks were recalibrated to thresholds that would make a Solarian engineer file an incident report. No weapons, no shields worth mentioning, no armor to speak of. Fast, cheap, and gets you there. It passes inspection because nobody on the Rim is looking that hard. Yet.

items.name: Tellurian
items.description: Solarian mining capital. Deploys mining drones autonomously, processes ore on-board. Pinnacle of industrial engineering.
items.lore: The Tellurian represents the pinnacle of Solarian industrial engineering. Its utility suite — the most extensive on any ship in the galaxy — supports autonomous mining drone deployment, real-time geological surveying, on-board ore processing, and quality assurance systems that operate without crew intervention. The ship identifies deposits, deploys extraction drones, processes the raw ore into refined materials, and stores the results in the 2,400-unit cargo bay. The entire operation runs autonomously according to algorithms refined over decades of geological research. The Confederacy considers the Tellurian its greatest industrial achievement. It is a mining operation in a hull.

items.name: Terms and Conditions
items.description: Outer Rim smuggler. Hidden compartments outnumber visible ones.
items.lore: Named for what you should have read before buying one, the Terms and Conditions features more hidden compartments than a magician's stage cabinet. Hull panels conceal cavities, life support ducting has removable sections, and the engine housing contains spaces that officially don't exist. The scan-resistant lining won't fool a dedicated customs cruiser, but it handles routine sweeps well enough to keep the interesting cargo off the manifest. When stealth fails, speed doesn't — most customs patrols can't match the Terms and Conditions in a straight chase, and Rim pilots know every shortcut between here and the next jurisdiction.

items.name: The Vault
items.description: Crimson armored bullion hauler — a T4 freighter wrapped in dreadnought-grade plating. No guns, no gadgets, no slots to fit any: just a hold, an engine, and enough armor to crawl past a pirate base and shrug off everything it throws. Slow as a glacier; arrives every time.
items.lore:
The Crimson Fleet does not, as a rule, build cargo ships — hauling is what you do
to the things you have already taken. The Vault is the exception they make for a
pilot rich enough to insult them with the commission, and they build it the only
way they know how: as armor with a hold bolted inside. The plating is darksteel
laid over fury-tempered plate over more darksteel, courses deep, until a boarding
crew's cutting charges run out before the hull does; raiders have been known to
knock on a Vault for the better part of a day and leave with nothing but a dented
reputation. All that mass has a price, and the price is paid in speed — the Vault
moves at a crawl, a slow gleaming brick grinding from port to port. Its owner does
not mind. When what you are moving is bullion, and the ship will arrive no matter
who objects, you can afford to be late.
items.prestige_lock: Locked: prestige hull reserved for pilots who have earned the "Bullion Baron" achievement.

items.name: Theorem
items.description: Solarian heavy fighter. Balanced combat platform with superior electronics.
items.lore: Where other empires bolt on more weapons, the Confederacy added more processing capacity. The Theorem carries the deepest fitting reserves of any heavy fighter in production — three open utility bays and enough CPU headroom for pilots to configure it for whatever the engagement demands. Escort duty, patrol interdiction, extended operations — same hull, different loadout. The engineering committee that approved the modular fitting architecture took eight months to reach consensus. The architecture then justified itself on the first deployment, in four configurations, across three theaters of operation.

items.name: Theoria
items.description: Solarian starter mining vessel. Certified, calibrated, warranty-covered.
items.lore:
Every Solarian pilot's journey begins with a Theoria. Named for the ancient
Greek concept of contemplative knowledge, this vessel embodies the Confederacy's
belief that understanding precedes action. The 300-page operations manual
(mandatory reading, examination required) covers everything from optimal ore
extraction angles to emergency hull breach poetry recitation protocols.
Over-engineered by three separate review committees, the Theoria has more
diagnostic systems than most ships have systems. The extended utility bus
accommodates the Confederacy's insistence that every vessel carry redundant
sensor packages. Comes with a two-year comprehensive warranty that covers
everything except "pilot-initiated misadventure."

items.name: Thermal Lance
items.description: Crimson deep-range ice breaker. Fuel-efficient drive reaches distant ice fields under armor.
items.lore: Ice fields worth harvesting at scale tend to be far from Fleet supply lines — deep frontier, contested space, places where shorter-range harvesters don't bother going. The Thermal Lance was built for that deployment. The fuel-efficient drive pushes the armored hull deep into territory that shorter-range harvesters avoid, and the dual thermal extractors work the ice while the autocannon keeps watch. The cargo hold is tight because the engineering committee prioritized fuel capacity and hull integrity over storage. Fleet ice operations run convoys for a reason — the Thermal Lance finds the field and cracks the ice. Someone else hauls it home.

items.name: Thermodynamic End
items.description: Voidborn capital salvager. Envelops entire capital wrecks and reduces them to sorted material streams.
items.lore:
The Thermodynamic End is the Collective's capital salvage vessel, named
for the principle it embodies: all ordered structures tend toward
dissolution, and the Collective merely accelerates the process. Its
organic hull can envelop an entire capital wreck, breaking it down into
sorted material streams over the course of hours. The vessel carries no
weapons — the shield envelope that protects it during salvage operations
has discouraged interference often enough that the Collective stopped
installing hardpoints entirely. The recovered materials emerge at a
purity that exceeds the original manufacturing specification, a result
that Solarian metallurgists have called "thermodynamically implausible."

items.name: Threshold
items.description: Voidborn starter vessel. Grown, not built. Anticipates pilot intent.
items.lore:
The Threshold is not manufactured. It is cultivated in Nexus Prime's orbital
growth bays over a period the Collective insists on calling "gestation." The
hull is a crystalline-organic composite that repairs microscopic fractures
autonomously. The shield generators draw power from sources the engineering
manual describes only as "adjacent." New pilots report that the ship
anticipates course corrections before they're input — the Collective
considers this a feature, not a concern. The cabin temperature is always
slightly wrong, regardless of thermostat settings. No Voidborn engineer
has ever acknowledged this as a defect.

items.name: Toll
items.description: Crimson customs enforcer. The price of crossing is inspection. The price of refusal is higher.
items.lore:
The Toll-class was designed by a committee that included both customs
officials and weapons engineers. The weapons engineers won most of the
arguments. Heavy armor and twin autocannons make the Toll significantly
overqualified for cargo inspection — which is, from the Crimson
perspective, exactly the point. Smugglers who encounter a Toll tend to
cooperate. Smugglers who encounter two Tolls tend to surrender. The
scanning suite is military-grade, because in the Crimson Pact, all
grades are military grades.

items.name: Treasury
items.description: Nebula luxury yacht. For captains who've earned the right to travel comfortably.
items.lore: The Treasury-class is the Federation's rolling advertisement for the rewards of commercial success. Panoramic viewports, climate-controlled cargo bays (for "delicate acquisitions"), and a passenger suite that would be excessive in a hotel. The three defense slots protect not just the hull but the lifestyle investment within. Five utility slots accommodate everything from entertainment systems to portfolio management terminals. The Federation offers financing at preferred customer rates.

items.name: Trebuchet
items.description: Crimson armored wall. A cheap slab of plating the Fleet parks in front of its guns to soak the incoming fire.
items.lore: The Trebuchet does not win battles. It survives them, which in Crimson accounting is the same thing measured from a different ledger. The hull is a slab of layered plating wrapped around almost nothing — a wall of armor with engines bolted to the back as an afterthought. Fleet doctrine parks it directly between the gunships and the enemy and tells the crew to hold position. Whatever fire would have shredded the real warships lands on the Trebuchet instead, and the Trebuchet absorbs it with the dull patience of a thing too stupid to know it is being shot. The two autocannons exist so the crew has something to do while they wait. Fleet engineers build it cheap and build it fast, because the role guarantees a short service life, and a wall that costs as much as a gunship is a wall nobody is willing to lose. The Fleet is always willing to lose a Trebuchet. That is the entire point.

items.name: Underwriter
items.description: Nebula convoy guard. Shield-heavy, long-range, and built to outlast threats.
items.lore:
The Federation calculated that purpose-built convoy guards cost 12% less
per annum than hired mercenaries, so they built one. The Underwriter's
160-unit fuel tank is the largest on any T1 combat hull — 53 jumps of
operational range before refueling, enough to shadow a trade convoy across
three systems and back. The shield-heavy defensive profile compensates for
light armor, keeping the ship functional through sustained engagements while
the cargo it's protecting reaches port. Fifty units of cargo space let pilots
recover salvage without calling for a hauler.

items.name: Vanguard
items.description: Crimson command ship. Leads from the front, not the rear. Fleet coordination through personal example.
items.lore: In most navies, the command ship sits behind the battle line. In the Crimson Fleet, a commander who leads from the rear is a commander who doesn't lead for long. The Vanguard carries fleet coordination systems powerful enough to manage a full battle group while simultaneously engaging targets with its own three weapon mounts. The extra defense slots exist not to protect the commander — Crimson commanders consider that cowardice — but to keep the coordination arrays functioning under fire. A Vanguard that stops transmitting because it took a hit costs the fleet more than one captain's pride is worth.

items.name: Venture
items.description: Nebula trade route scout. Finds new markets and brings samples home.
items.lore: The Venture-class was designed for the Federation's market development division: find new systems, assess their commercial potential, bring samples back for valuation. The fuel reserves support 60-jump survey runs deep into unmapped space, and the cargo hold — the largest on any exploration platform — means the scout returns with enough material for proper market analysis, not just sensor readings. The open weapon slot and defense mount acknowledge that unmapped space is not always empty, and the fitting budget lets pilots configure for the risk profile of each survey run. The operations manual opens with: "Discovery is just commerce that hasn't happened yet."

items.name: Verglas
items.description: Voidborn anomalous ice harvester. Phase-shifts through ice to extract materials from deep cores.
items.lore:
The Verglas-class harvests ice through dimensional phase-shifting
at capital scale. The extraction system reaches through the surface of
ice bodies without disturbing them, pulling target materials directly
from deep cores that conventional equipment cannot access. Nine hundred
shield points protect against the dimensional stress of sustained
phase-extraction operations. The technique is unique to the Voidborn —
other empires lack the dimensional technology to reach into solid
matter without breaking it. The Collective considers this approach
both more efficient and more respectful of the ice body's structural
integrity.

items.name: Vigil
items.description: Voidborn patrol vessel. Shield-hardened enforcement platform that outlasts anything it encounters.
items.lore: A vigil is a period of watchful attention — and the Collective considers enforcement to be exactly that. The Vigil-class carries layered shield generators that let it absorb sustained fire while its twin pulse lasers methodically dismantle non-compliant vessels. Voidborn patrol doctrine does not emphasize pursuit or intimidation. The Vigil was already in position before you arrived. It has been watching since before you noticed it. The integrated sensor suite confirms what the Collective already suspected, and the shields ensure the conversation lasts as long as necessary. Resistance is technically an option. The shields make it a poor one.

items.name: Voidborn Event Horizon
items.description: Voidborn battlecruiser. The boundary beyond which nothing escapes.
items.lore:
The Event Horizon earns its name. Its shield array creates a zone of
absolute energy absorption around the hull — weapons fire enters but
does not exit as reflected energy. Other empires' tactical analysts
describe engaging an Event Horizon as "firing into a black hole."
The weapon complement is secondary by design: the Event Horizon does
not need to destroy its targets quickly. It needs to outlast them.
Five defense slots support the most comprehensive shield architecture
mounted on anything smaller than a capital ship. Fleet intelligence
reports suggest the power systems draw from dimensional micro-fractures,
producing sustained output that should not be possible from a reactor
this size.

items.name: Voidborn Singularity
items.description: Voidborn cruiser. Shield layers that shouldn't be possible. Crew reports mild temporal displacement.
items.lore: The Singularity-class carries shield arrays that produce readings other empires' sensors classify as "errors." Four defense slots support a layered shield architecture that the Collective describes as "recursive probability reduction." Enemy weapons officers report that targeting solutions decay faster than they can be computed. Crew members occasionally experience mild deja vu, which the ship's manual lists under "features" rather than "known issues."

items.name: War Wagon
items.description: Crimson bulk hauler. The biggest hold below the heavy tiers, bolted to an engine that resents the work. Crawls, holds everything, defends nothing.
items.lore: Calling the War Wagon a ship flatters it. It is a warehouse that the Fleet talked into having an engine, and the engine has regretted the conversation ever since. The hold swallows cargo on a scale that embarrasses proper haulers, and that hold is the entire ship — everything else is the minimum framework needed to keep the load from drifting off and the minimum thrust needed to move the whole resentful mass from one parking orbit to the next, slowly, with the dignity of a glacier. There is armor, technically. There are no guns, and nobody pretends the two plates will matter once someone decides the War Wagon is worth the trouble of shooting. The Fleet doesn't sortie it. The Fleet parks it: at a forward depot, behind the line, full to the bulkheads, and waits for the day the supplies are needed more than the wagon is safe. Quartermasters love it. Captains avoid it. Both are correct.

items.name: Warbarge
items.description: Crimson armored fleet tanker. Wars run on fuel; the Warbarge runs the fuel.
items.lore: Wars run on fuel, and the Warbarge runs the fuel. The Crimson Pact's heaviest tanker carries enough bunkerage to sustain a strike group through a multi-system campaign without resupply, and is armored to make sure it arrives. Two autocannon batteries are not enough to repel a serious threat, but they are enough to convince the casual opportunist that there are easier targets in the system. Pact doctrine assigns Warbarges their own escort wings on the principle that the loss of a Warbarge ends the operation it serves: the math is simpler than commanders like to admit. The captain receives standing orders to ram any boarding ship that breaches the perimeter, on the grounds that a Warbarge lost in transit is worth less than the same Warbarge lost on arrival. Pact accountants have done the calculation and signed off.

items.name: Warhammer
items.description: Crimson bulk salvager. Dual cargo expanders, maximum haul per wreck site. Brings everything home.
items.lore: The Crimson Fleet produces more wrecks than any other empire, and leaving salvage on the field wastes materiel. The Warhammer ships with dual cargo expanders for raw haul volume and the fitting budget left over gives pilots real choices — mount a weapon, add armor, extend the fuel range. That flexibility matters because the stock fuel tank is short. This is a local operations ship, built to strip wreck sites in Crimson space and haul everything home in one trip. The tow rating won't win any races, but when a wreck field has more loot than a lighter salvager can carry, the Warhammer earns its name. Fleet recycling doctrine: what was theirs is ours.

items.name: Warhead
items.description: Crimson armored hauler. What the Fleet carries in these is not your business. The armor ensures this.
items.lore:
Isotope shipments moving under Fleet protection kept being boarded,
inspected, and — on two occasions — destroyed. The Fleet considered
all three outcomes unacceptable. The Warhead-class was the response:
two weapon mounts, warship-grade armor certified to active combat
standards, and a lead-lined cargo bay rated to Fleet ordnance
specifications, which exceed civilian equivalents by a margin other
empires are not permitted to audit. The name was assigned by the
Fleet's logistics records department without review. Commanders
transporting reactor fuel note on transit manifests that the ship
class is named Warhead, not the cargo. This distinction has
prevented three confirmed intercept responses from empires whose
scanner operators were paying close attention. It continues to
require noting.

items.name: Warmaul
items.description: Crimson main battle cruiser. Five weapon mounts. The backbone of any serious Crimson operation.
items.lore: The Warmaul is where the Crimson Fleet stops pretending and starts deploying. Five weapon mounts deliver sustained broadside firepower that exceeds anything else at this scale. The armor is thick enough to wade through fighter screens without flinching. The power grid runs all five weapons without compromise. Multi-role is for ships that aren't sure what they're for. The Warmaul is a gun platform that happens to have engines. Fleet commanders consider it the minimum acceptable response to any tactical situation. Everything lighter is "reconnaissance in force."

items.name: Warranty
items.description: Nebula repair vessel. Keeping Federation assets in service is cheaper than replacing them.
items.lore: The Warranty-class is the Federation's mobile maintenance platform, because every hour a damaged freighter sits idle is revenue lost. Five utility slots accommodate repair drones, hull printers, and diagnostic arrays. The generous cargo bay stores replacement parts at markup prices. The Federation offers "Warranty Extended Service Contracts" that guarantee priority repair — terms and conditions apply.

items.name: Warranty Void
items.description: Outer Rim explorer. Goes further than intended on less fuel than expected.
items.lore: Named for its relationship with every manufacturer whose parts went into its construction, the Warranty Void is built for pilots who believe the map's edge is a suggestion. The fuel system extracts more range from every cell through techniques that void approximately seventeen different safety certifications, and the default afterburner lets pilots choose: burn fast at Speed 6 for short dashes, or pull the afterburner and cruise at Speed 5 for runs that reach the far side of the galaxy. No defense slots and minimal armor — the survival strategy is not getting caught, and at Speed 6, most things can't catch you. Rim explorers don't report their modifications. They report their discoveries.

items.name: Waystation
items.description: Nebula mobile fleet depot. Carries more ships than most stations park.
items.lore: The Federation conducted a seventeen-system audit of inter-system transit costs and concluded that empty ships traveling back to their pilots represented the single largest preventable expense in small-fleet logistics. The Waystation-class was the solution: twelve bay slots, enough cargo for a working run, and zero weapon mounts because the credits saved on armament were better spent on bay reinforcement. A Waystation pays for itself in approximately fourteen return trips avoided. The Federation has calculated this precisely. They mention the calculation often.

items.name: Workhorse
items.description: A lean faction utility hull that mines, hauls, and scouts in one frame — efficient to run and competent at each, so a small crew wastes no ships.
items.lore:
A lean operation cannot afford a dedicated hull for every task, so the Workhorse
does three. It carries a mining laser, a real hold, and a scanner, runs cheap on
fuel, and stretches a cargo bay further than its size suggests. It is not the
best miner, the best hauler, or the best scout — a specialist beats it at each —
but a specialist sits idle between jobs, and the Workhorse never does. Issued to
crews small enough that everyone aboard is expected to do a little of everything,
and large enough to have earned the right to do it well.
items.prestige_lock: Locked: prestige hull reserved for members of a faction that has earned the "Lean Operation" achievement.

items.name: Worship
items.description: Outer Rim cargo hauler, usually ordered by mistake. A surprisingly effective hauler if you decline to consider the loss rate.
items.lore:
Usually ordered because of poor handwriting, the Worship turns out to be
a surprisingly effective cargo hauler — provided you decline to consider
the loss rate. It is generally considered uninsurable, and yet it still
makes up a substantial fraction of the cargo traffic in the rougher parts
of the Rim, moving goods nobody was willing to risk a real ship on. It is
often mistaken for four Prayers welded together. This is inaccurate. It is
actually just tape.

items.name: Yard Sale
items.description: Outer Rim wreck tug. One job — drag dead hulls home without making you quit.
items.lore: Stubby, slow, and built around a tow rig the size of the cockpit, the Yard Sale exists for exactly one job and is no good at anything else. Drag a dead hull or a fat wreck across three systems in anything else and you will spend the whole crawl wondering why you chose this life. Drag it in a Yard Sale and the load barely registers — the tug hauls a wreck near enough to its own speed that the trip stops being punishment and starts being just another haul. There is no clever second use here. It cannot fight, it cannot run, it cannot carry much of its own. What it can do is grab something three times its mass that nobody else wants to move and bring it home, and on the Rim that turns out to be worth a hull all by itself.

items.name: Yield
items.description: Nebula gas harvester. Industrial gas compression halves collected volume for maximum extraction efficiency.
items.lore: The Federation's gas extraction division ran the numbers on fuel costs versus nebula accessibility and arrived at the Yield-class: a harvester with the longest fuel range in its class by a wide margin. Competitors harvest the easy nebulae close to trade lanes. The Yield harvests everything else. The single default harvester and open fitting give pilots room to customize for whatever the deep-range run demands. The hull won't survive a fight, but the Federation prefers routes where fights don't happen.
